Theorem
[Continuity method for nonlinear boundary operators] 1. ch17:17.28\group chapter-17Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0495 Let $\Omega $ be a $C^{2,\alpha }$ domain, $0<\alpha <1$, let $\mathcal U\subset C^{2,\alpha }(\overline\Omega )$ be open, and fix $\psi \in \mathcal U$. Set \begin{equation} \tag {17.105} E=\{ u\in \mathcal U:P[u]=\sigma P[\psi ] \text{ for some }\sigma \in [0,1]\} . \end{equation} Assume $F\in C^{2,\alpha }(\overline\Gamma )$, $G\in C^{3,\alpha }(\Gamma ')$, and

  1. $F$ is strictly elliptic with respect to every $u\in E$;

  2. for every $u\in E$, $G$ is either Dirichlet, $G(x,z,p)=z-\phi (x)$, or is oblique with respect to $u$;

  3. $F_z(x,u,Du,D^2u)\le 0$ and $G_z(x,u,Du)\ge 0$ for every $u\in E$, and the two functions are not both identically zero;

  4. $E$ is bounded in $C^{2,\alpha }(\overline\Omega )$;

  5. $\overline E\subset \mathcal U$.

Then (17.100) has a solution in $\mathcal U$.
Proof

\sketch Linear oblique Schauder theory makes (17.104) invertible under (i)–(iii). Theorem 20 makes the continuation set open; (iv)–(v) and compactness make it closed. Theorem 21 finishes the homotopy.

□

For the remaining results let \begin{equation} \tag {17.106} Qu=a^{ij}(x,u,Du)D_{ij}u+b(x,u,Du). \end{equation}
